messages:
ana: quick question — I have request_id=req_5f1a2b3c and need the raw log lines + any linked trace. fastest way: console or CLI?
kevin: console if you want quick clicks: Observability -> Logs, then filter with `request_id:\"req_5f1a2b3c\"`. set view to JSON/raw to see full payload. Traces -> paste trace id if you have it.
maria: if you only have a trace id, you can open Traces -> search -> trace_7f8e9a -> pick a span -> Attributes -> request_id.
kevin: CLI option (my go-to for copies):
```
rwdctl logs query --filter 'request_id=req_5f1a2b3c' --start -30m --limit 500 --raw
```
or for streaming: `rwdctl logs tail --request-id req_5f1a2b3c --env prod`
darren: heads up — some older services didn't set request_id in logs, they only set `x-request-id` or put it on the span. if the direct request_id lookup returns nothing, try a trace->span attr lookup or search `http.request_id` / `x-request-id`.
kevin: mapping trace->request via CLI: `rwdctl traces get trace_7f8e9a --fields spans.attributes` and grep for request_id. console link if you want to share: https://console.redwood.ai/traces/trace_7f8e9a
maria: small note for the runbook: include the `--raw` flag to avoid truncation, and example filters. i'll PR the cheatsheet after lunch.
nana? ana: got it, found the logs + trace, thanks! :thumbsup:
obs-bot: [alert] high-latency /infer at 1819002000 (for context)
kevin: if you escalate to support include both the request_id and the trace link + the `rwdctl` output you used. that speeds triage.
maria: also recommend adding a shell alias for interns: `alias rlogs='rwdctl logs query --start -60m --limit 200'` — keeps them from overloading queries.
darren: one more tip — if you need to correlate across services, use `--start`/`--end` to limit window and `--raw` to get structured fields.
nana? ana: pinging ops to request rwdctl scopes for the new hires so they can run these commands.
